page: Amazon Web Services u7in-24tb.224xlarge is an enterprise-scale, memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It features Intel x86_64 processors running at a clock speed of 1.9 GHz, providing 448 physical cores and 896 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. The hardware architecture contains zero discrete GPUs, prioritizing CPU compute and high memory allocation.

The primary differentiator of the server is its 24,576 GB system memory allocation, yielding 27.43 GB of RAM per physical core. This high-density memory profile enables massive datasets to reside fully in volatile storage. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistence. External connectivity is backed by 200 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, supporting high-throughput transfer across clustered resources and network storage volumes.

From a cost-efficiency and performance perspective, this server enables significant vertical consolidation for workloads that would otherwise require complex distributed systems. A primary hardware tradeoff is the total reliance on network-attached storage and the absence of GPU acceleration. Consequently, the u7in-24tb.224xlarge is designed for large-scale enterprise in-memory databases, production SAP HANA installations, and high-throughput in-memory analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services u7in-24tb.224xlarge is a high-memory Nitro-based instance designed for extreme-scale in-memory compute workloads. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the server is powered by Intel processors running at 1.9 GHz, offering 448 physical cores across 896 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. The defining attribute of this instance is its 24,576 GB memory footprint, which delivers 27.43 GB of RAM per physical core to support exceptionally large data footprints directly in volatile memory. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 200 Gbps for high-throughput distributed operations. The instance includes no local storage, requiring architectures to leverage external network volumes such as Amazon EBS. There are no discrete GPUs provisioned on this configuration. Given its substantial hardware footprint, the instance consolidates computing resources for enterprise deployments such as massive SAP HANA environments, large in-memory databases, and high-volume real-time transactional or analytical processing pipelines.
